findings.title: Comment miscites RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND for the docs-build skip mechanism
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:26 — "A round of a docs instrument freezes the build (`RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND`)."
.gbg/policy/instruments.md (RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND) — "An instrument is never changed mid-round; a change is its own commit and release"
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:2304 — sentinel "An instrument is never changed mid-round; a change is its own commit and release."
findings.description: The comment cites RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND as the reason the docs build is skipped while a check-docs/check-consistency round is open. But that rule's actual content (confirmed identically in the rendered policy and in ARCHITECTURE.md's sentinel table) governs a different thing: an instrument's own definition (its scans, scripts, catalogue) may not be edited while a round using it is open. It says nothing about a docs build being refused or skipped because a round is merely open — that behavior is gate()/frozen_rounds()'s own design (Gate.jl: 'A build refused ONLY for these is frozen, not broken'), not an instance of FROZEN_MIDROUND. No other citation of RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND in the source ties it to build-skipping; the only other hit (Passes.jl:713, carrying deferrals into the work queue) matches the rule's real meaning. This is a false citation of a specific, load-bearing rule id in a codebase where rule ids are meant to be traceable one-to-one to RULES.toml.
findings.resolution_hint: Either drop the parenthetical rule-id citation and just describe the mechanism in the wrapper's own terms (point to frozen_rounds/gate instead), or, if a policy rule is wanted, name one that actually governs closure discipline rather than instrument immutability — FROZEN_MIDROUND is not it.

findings.title: Module docstring uses the term of art "consumer" unglossed and unlinked
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:5 — "the mandatory wrapper a consumer's `docs/make.jl` calls"
src/GBGCodingTools.jl:7 — "A consumer is a package that uses the tool — one of the four sibling GBG packages, or the tool itself."
src/DocLints.jl:10-13 — the sibling home docstring for the same makedocs operation defines 'instrument'/'round' inline and links [`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) on first use
findings.description: "Consumer" is one of the package's bound terms of art (defined once, in GBGCodingTools's own module docstring: "A consumer is a package that uses the tool"). The ext module docstring uses it at its first mention ("a consumer's docs/make.jl calls") with no defining clause and no @ref link back to the module that binds it, failing the cold-read test RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED sets. This is the same docstring's own sibling — src/DocLints.jl's home docstring for the identical makedocs operation — which does exactly this for 'instrument' and 'round', explicitly linking [`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) as the term's home. The ext module docstring breaks that established pattern for 'consumer'.
findings.resolution_hint: Add [`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) at consumer's first mention (e.g. "the mandatory wrapper a [`consumer`](@ref GBGCodingTools)'s docs/make.jl calls") or a short parenthetical, matching DocLints.jl's practice for the same function.

findings.title: check()'s docstring signature omits the method's argument types
findings.description: RULE.DOC.SIGNATURE_MIRROR requires the docstring's shown signature to mirror the method's types ("An argument typed in the method is typed in the docstring"). The method declares verb::AbstractString and code::Integer, but the docstring's code block shows the untyped check(verb, code), so a reader copying the shown signature would not see the actual type constraints.
findings.resolution_hint: Change the docstring's signature line to check(verb::AbstractString, code::Integer).
